content.value_statement: React Native teams need fast, reliable tests for components, hooks, utilities, and forms. This skill gives Jest and React Native Testing Library patterns for setup, mocks, async tests, and failure debugging.
actual_capabilities: Guides Jest setup for React Native projects, including common test scripts.
Provides component, hook, and utility test patterns with React Native Testing Library.
Shows mocks for notifications, database clients, and Expo Router navigation.
Explains commands for all tests, watch mode, coverage, specific files, and snapshot updates.
Helps troubleshoot timeouts, missing elements, mocks, and async test failures.
limitations: It is a guide, not a test runner by itself.
It does not replace project-specific Jest configuration review.
It does not cover native end-to-end frameworks such as Detox or Maestro.
Examples may need changes for custom aliases, providers, or navigation setup.

use_cases.title: Add Component Coverage
use_cases.description: A React Native developer creates behavior-focused tests for buttons, forms, lists, and loading states.

use_cases.title: Prepare Test Infrastructure
use_cases.description: A mobile tech lead sets up Jest scripts, dependencies, mocks, and coverage checks for a new project.

use_cases.title: Debug Failing Tests
use_cases.description: A QA automation engineer investigates async failures, missing elements, and unstable mocks in a mobile test suite.

prompt_templates.title: Create First Component Test
prompt_templates.prompt: Write a React Native Testing Library test for this component. Focus on visible behavior and press interactions.

prompt_templates.title: Add Hook and Utility Tests
prompt_templates.prompt: Create Jest tests for this hook and utility module. Include normal, error, and edge cases.

prompt_templates.title: Mock App Dependencies
prompt_templates.prompt: Set up mocks for Expo Router, notifications, and the database client. Explain where each mock should live.

prompt_templates.title: Stabilize a Test Suite
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these failing React Native tests. Identify async, mock, and selector issues, then propose minimal fixes.

output_examples.input: A button component with title and press handler props.
output_examples.output: A component test plan that renders the title, presses the button, and verifies one callback call.

output_examples.input: A login form test that cannot find the email field.
output_examples.output: A debugging checklist covering test identifiers, rendered output inspection, mock import order, and async query choices.

output_examples.input: A mobile app project without Jest scripts.
output_examples.output: A setup plan with required packages, script purposes, coverage workflow, and watch workflow.

best_practices: Test user-visible behavior before implementation details.
Use stable test identifiers when text can change.
Mock external services so tests stay fast and deterministic.
anti_patterns: Do not assert private component state when visible behavior is available.
Do not mix real network services into unit tests.
Do not update snapshots without reviewing the user-facing change.

faq.question: Does this skill run tests automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides commands and test patterns that a user or agent can apply in the project.

faq.question: Which frameworks does it cover?
faq.answer: It focuses on Jest and React Native Testing Library for React Native applications.

faq.question: Can it help with Expo projects?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes Expo Router and Expo notification mock patterns that can be adapted.

faq.question: Does it cover end-to-end testing?
faq.answer: No. It does not provide Detox, Appium, or Maestro workflows.

faq.question: Can it improve test reliability?
faq.answer: Yes. It recommends isolated mocks, async queries, and focused assertions to reduce flaky tests.

faq.question: Is it suitable for beginners?
faq.answer: Yes. It starts with component tests and grows into mocks, async testing, and troubleshooting.
